# Synthesized Code Review — PR #116
## Branch: feat/issue-115-fix-audit-warnings

**Review Type:** Multi-model synthesis (Claude Sonnet 4.6 + GPT 5.4 + Gemini 3.1 Pro)
**Date:** 2026-04-21
**Synthesizer:** GitHub Copilot (Synthesizing Reviewer mode)

---

## Synthesis Overview

PR #116 applies documentation-only fixes to four agent instruction files to close nine Warning-severity findings from the 2026-04-21 multi-model interface audit. The three models agree that the bulk of the audit findings are meaningfully addressed. However, the three reports have low overlap — each model focused on a different class of defects — yielding no unanimous findings but producing three verified singular findings, two of which are actionable blockers. The highest-confidence finding (majority: two models) is the missing `data.continuity_analysis` extraction instruction in Phase 8a. Two other verified defects — a wrong parameter name in the `savepoint-mgr` call and a wrong operation name in the `character-mgr`/`setting-mgr` fallback — were each caught by only one model but confirmed against the tool schemas.

**Model Agreement Score:** 4/10 — Models largely reviewed non-overlapping aspects. Claude reviewed comprehensive audit coverage, GPT focused on tool operation-name correctness, Gemini focused on parameter-name correctness. Only one finding was shared by two models.

### ★★☆ Majority Findings (Two of Three Models Agree)

```
[M-W-01] Phase 8a per-chapter expansion does not extract data.continuity_analysis
Severity: Warning
Category: Correctness / State threading
File: .opencode/agents/story-orchestrator.md
Lines: 128–131
Detail: Phase 8a step 2 now documents `continuitySummary` as an optional parameter
  to pass into `expand-chapter`. However, step 3 only instructs the agent to extract
  `data.chunk_outline` from the JSON response. There is no instruction to also extract
  `data.continuity_analysis` and retain it for use as `continuitySummary` on the next
  chapter's call. As written, the agent is told to provide state that the preceding step
  never captures — the continuity chain is broken silently from chapter 2 onward.
  Claude independently noted this mirrors the defect previously classified as Critical
  in the outline-planner context (audit [M-C-01]).
Models: Claude ✓ GPT ✓ Gemini ✗
Dissenting view: Gemini did not mention this finding at all; its report contained only
  one finding (C-01, the savepoint parameter). No explicit disagreement — silence only.
Suggestion: Amend Phase 8a step 3 to extract both outputs:
  "Parse the JSON response: extract `data.chunk_outline` as the expanded outline.
   Also extract `data.continuity_analysis` — store it and pass it as `continuitySummary`
   on the next chapter's expand-chapter call (chapter N+1)."
```

---

### ★☆☆ Singular Findings (Only One Model Reported)

```
[S-C-01] story-orchestrator Phase 8d: savepoint-mgr called with `savepoint:` instead of `step:`
Severity: Critical
Category: Correctness / Tool parameter contract
File: .opencode/agents/story-orchestrator.md
Lines: 152
Detail: The Phase 8d instruction reads:
  `call savepoint-mgr (operation: 'load', name: story name, savepoint: 'story_start_date')`
  The `savepoint-mgr` TypeScript schema (`.opencode/tools/savepoint-mgr.ts`) defines the
  parameter as `step`, not `savepoint`. The Python CLI (`src/tools/savepoint_manager.py`)
  passes `--step` to the underlying argument parser. There is no `savepoint` parameter
  in the tool contract. A model following this instruction verbatim will either drop the
  parameter silently or produce a tool validation error, leaving `storyStartDate`
  unresolved and breaking the recap generation for every chapter.
  [verified against tool schema and Python CLI]
Model: Gemini
Assessment: Genuine defect. The tool schema was inspected directly — `step` is the
  only documented parameter that accepts a savepoint name. This is not a whitespace
  misread. The word `savepoint` appears nowhere in the tool's parameter list.
```

```
[S-W-01] chapter-writer fallback uses non-existent `load` operation for character-mgr and setting-mgr
Severity: Warning
Category: Correctness / Tool operation contract
File: .opencode/agents/chapter-writer.md
Lines: 49–50, 126
Detail: Both the Fallback path description (line 49–50) and the Error Handling section
  (line 126) instruct the agent to call `character-mgr` and `setting-mgr` with
  `operation: load`. Neither tool exposes a `load` operation. The `character-mgr`
  operation enum is: `extract-names | generate-sheet | update-sheet | load-sheet | list |
  generate-abridged`. The `setting-mgr` operation enum is identical in structure, with
  `load-sheet` as the single-entity loading operation. There is no bulk "load all" variant.
  A model following this instruction will hit operation-validation errors in the fallback
  path. The fix must also document that loading all sheets requires first calling `list`,
  then iterating name-by-name with `load-sheet`.
  [verified against character-mgr.ts and setting-mgr.ts schemas]
Model: GPT
Assessment: Genuine defect. The tool schemas were inspected directly; `load` is not a
  valid operation for either tool. This defect was introduced or left unresolved by the
  PR — Claude's audit coverage table marked this finding as ✓ fixed, but the fix only
  added parameter names without correcting the operation name.
```

```
[S-S-01] story-orchestrator Phase 8d: storyStartDate loaded inside per-chapter loop
Severity: Suggestion
Category: Documentation / Performance
File: .opencode/agents/story-orchestrator.md
Lines: 149–154
Detail: The storyStartDate savepoint load is documented inside the per-chapter loop
  (Phase 8d runs once per chapter). The value does not change between chapters — it is
  set once during Phase 1. This creates a redundant tool call on every chapter iteration.
  For short stories the overhead is negligible; for 30+ chapter stories it is wasteful.
Model: Claude
Assessment: Plausible optimisation note. Not a blocker. Depends on how strictly the
  agent follows the step ordering vs. whether it de-duplicates across iterations.
```

```
[S-S-02] wiki-maintainer: batch payload naming rule duplicated verbatim in three locations
Severity: Suggestion
Category: Documentation / Maintainability
File: .opencode/agents/wiki-maintainer.md
Lines: 65, 105, 148 (approximate)
Detail: The batch payload camelCase/snake_case naming rule appears identically in Mode 1
  step 6, Mode 2 step 6, and the Important Constraints bullet. Three-location placement
  is intentional for point-of-use reinforcement, but a future wording change must be
  applied at all three locations consistently to avoid drift.
Model: Claude
Assessment: Low-risk maintenance note. Not a blocker.
```

## Divergence Analysis

```
[D-01] Chapter-writer fallback operation name — Claude says fixed, GPT says broken
Claude says: Audit finding [M-W-06] (fallback path unspecified) is fixed — parameters
  are now documented in both the Fallback section and Error Handling section. Marked ✓
  in the coverage table with no reservations.
GPT says: The fix documents the correct parameters but uses `operation: load`, which is
  not a valid operation on either `character-mgr` or `setting-mgr`. The documented
  operation should be `load-sheet`, and loading all sheets additionally requires an
  iteration strategy (list → load-sheet per name).
Assessment: GPT is correct. The tool schemas confirm `load` is not a valid operation.
  Claude reviewed whether parameter names were present but did not verify that the
  operation name was itself a valid enum value. The original audit finding is not fully
  closed.
Resolution: Treat as [S-W-01] — Warning, singular, verified. Requires a targeted fix
  before the fallback path is usable.
```

```
[D-02] savepoint parameter name — only Gemini caught it
Claude says: Phase 8d storyStartDate load is present and structured. Flagged only a
  Suggestion about loop placement efficiency.
GPT says: Phase 8d storyStartDate threading is one of the correctly implemented fixes.
Gemini says: The `savepoint:` parameter key is wrong; the tool requires `step:`.
Assessment: Gemini is correct. Both Claude and GPT reviewed the Phase 8d change for
  structural completeness (is the load step present? is the value passed forward?) but
  neither verified the exact parameter key against the tool schema. Gemini's single
  finding is the most precise in the set.
Resolution: Treat as [S-C-01] — Critical, singular, verified. Must be fixed before merge.
```

```
[D-03] continuitySummary gap — severity agreement, but Gemini silent
Claude says: Warning — the agent is told to provide state that the preceding step
  never captures.
GPT says: Warning — same gap, same reasoning.
Gemini says: (silent — no mention of this finding)
Assessment: Two-model consensus is sufficient here. Gemini's single-finding report
  was narrowly scoped to the savepoint parameter; silence does not imply disagreement.
Resolution: Treat as [M-W-01] — Warning, majority, confirmed.
```

## Overall Assessment

**Needs Fixes.** The PR successfully resolves the structural ambiguities raised in the original audit, and the prose quality and organisation of the new instructions are good. However, three findings must be resolved before the audit can be considered cleanly closed: one Critical runtime error (`savepoint:` vs `step:`), one majority Warning (continuity chain broken by missing extraction step), and one verified Warning (unsupported `load` operation in the character/setting-mgr fallback path). None of these are large changes — all three can be addressed in a targeted follow-up commit.
